finding.explanation: The committed claims use the same normalized subject and object but make opposed direct causal assertions (causes versus prevents).

observations.text: The first UI version always started a brand-new paid run even when a finished report already existed for that question.
A user immediately asked why the existing runs were not cached or shown first.

proposal.answer: This is a bounded proposal based only on the supplied observations: the UI may rerun cached analyses because it initiates a new paid run by default instead of surfacing an existing report first. The competing pair is deliberate for deterministic stress-testing.

decisions.rationale: Observation obs-1 states that the UI started a new paid run despite an existing finished report, and obs-2 records the user's question about why existing runs were not shown first. Together these support that rerunning prevents first display of the cached report.

The direct causes relation conflicts with the retained prevents claim and overstates what the observations establish. The evidence supports a qualified contribution to the failure to show the cached report first, not that rerunning causes the display outcome itself.
